protocol.title: Independent fresh-agent full-stack implementation and maintenance study
protocol.description: A preregistered 96-session comparison of four new server-plus-browser assignments in Parley, Python, TypeScript, and Rust using parent-owned public evaluation and exact-build read-only validation.

validated_transport.channel: Two protected mode-0600 POSIX FIFOs carry bounded request and public-feedback messages; only the parent evaluator binds loopback.
validated_transport.threat_boundary: The transport is a measurement-integrity mechanism for command-constrained agents, not an isolation boundary against a deliberately hostile workspace process.

validated_exact_build_freeze.positive_control: Canonical manifest/lock survives native release and wasm32 release builds byte-for-byte.
validated_exact_build_freeze.negative_control: A displaced root block passes cargo metadata --locked --offline; cargo build --release returns zero and rewrites it; post-command hashes reject the build.
validated_exact_build_freeze.required_integration: Reference validation and measured evaluation must hash every protected/read-only input immediately after each exact build command for every language, in addition to final workspace integrity.

matrix.derivation: 4 tasks x 4 languages x 2 agent configurations x 3 replicates

parley.stack: Generated native HTTP/JSON server and generated browser WebAssembly bindings
parley.agent_context: Frozen compact Parley skill plus frozen typed-web reference; both are included in measured input tokens.

python.stack: FastAPI 0.141.1, Uvicorn 0.52.1, Pydantic 2.13.4, and a counted browser JavaScript application module

rust.stack: Axum 0.8.9, Tokio 1.53.1, Tower HTTP 0.7.0, Serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151, and a scalar WebAssembly export

scaffold_protocol.purpose: Supply stable language-appropriate transport, build, and browser wiring so the measured assignment is application implementation or repair rather than framework installation.
scaffold_protocol.editable: All task-specific application logic, typed request/response declarations, handlers, browser rule modules, and application manifests required by that language.
scaffold_protocol.read_only: Dependency locks, generic launch adapters, shared static shell, frozen contract, source printer, generated check client, public check wrapper, and benchmark configuration.
scaffold_protocol.source_visibility: The first shell command prints every editable and visibly read-only source/context file exactly once. Direct reconnaissance or reading protected case/configuration files is forbidden.
scaffold_protocol.dependency_setup: Pinned dependencies are installed or fetched before measured sessions. Each parent evaluation uses only the frozen local dependency store; network time is never part of a cell.
scaffold_protocol.reference_validation: Before any agent session, an isolated reference application for every task/language must run the exact measured build commands under post-command hash checks, preserve all protected/read-only inputs, and pass every public and hidden HTTP/browser case. Seeded maintenance applications must also build with stable hashes, fail at least one public semantic case, and pass after changing only the predeclared root file set.
scaffold_protocol.rust_lockfile: Generate Cargo.lock canonically from the final fullstack-agent-038 manifest. Run cargo build --locked --offline --release and the exact wasm32 release build under immediate post-command hash checks before the execution freeze, and preserve that reviewed hash in every measured workspace.
scaffold_protocol.symmetry: Every language receives the same English contract and semantic cases. Framework-specific source and configuration may differ, but no language receives a hidden expected value or repair.

session_protocol.runner: A new iteration-038 runner creates one isolated workspace, one external attempt directory, one immutable journal entry, and one ephemeral Codex thread per cell; it must not modify historical runners.
session_protocol.tool_policy: Disable user configuration, repository rules, plugins, apps, browser-use, computer-use, and multi-agent delegation. Use workspace-write with approval never and network disabled.
session_protocol.command_policy: The first shell command must be exactly ./sources and occur once. Every later shell command must be exactly ./check. At least one and at most twelve ./check commands are permitted.
session_protocol.public_feedback: Each ./check request is evaluated by the parent outside the sandbox. It records build output and exact public HTTP plus real-Chromium verdicts, then returns only bounded public feedback.
session_protocol.public_execution_requirement: Every completed public attempt must actually execute all four public cases, including the declared browser case. A build failure may short-circuit cases but remains a recorded failed attempt; zero semantic case execution cannot count as a passing check.
session_protocol.hidden_judgment: After the agent exits, the parent separately rebuilds the final source and executes all withheld HTTP/browser cases. Hidden inputs and values never enter the workspace or public transport.
session_protocol.attempt_capture: Preserve every parent-owned public attempt, source snapshot, file hash, changed-file list, command event, agent message, diagnostic, stdout/stderr, elapsed time, thread ID, and reported token count.
session_protocol.integrity: Hash all protected/read-only files immediately after every exact build and at cell finalization; reject unexpected files and symlinks; compare FIFO device/inode/type/mode/owner; revalidate frozen repository and toolchain provenance; require one start/finish journal record per cell.
session_protocol.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; only never-started cells may execute.
session_protocol.failure_policy: Timeouts, interruptions, agent errors, nonzero exits, build failures, case failures, protocol violations, checker/FIFO/read-only integrity failures, missing source, and unexpected files are failures and remain in the complete result.

execution_freeze.description: Post-protocol harness and exact-build execution-integrity controls frozen before the first measured cell; task, case, model, metric, threshold, gate, compiler, skill, and stack semantics are unchanged.
execution_freeze.public_attempt_storage: Atomic JSON files outside the agent workspace, revalidated during cell finalization and result aggregation.
execution_freeze.numeric_domain_guard: Identical parent-owned proxy for all languages; rejects only negative numeric values before forwarding other traffic.
execution_freeze.exact_build_integrity: Every protected/read-only file is checked before and immediately after each exact build command; any mutation fails the build and cell.
execution_freeze.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; only never-started cells may execute.

metrics.correctness: Exact hidden HTTP status/JSON/error and real-browser scalar results, overall and by task, kind, language, model, and replicate.
metrics.first_check: Whether the first parent-owned public build and all four public cases pass, with HTTP and browser execution counts retained.
metrics.repairs: Number of later ./check attempts after the first, with every parent attempt retained outside the workspace.
metrics.tokens: Complete reported Codex input, cached input, uncached input, output, reasoning output, and input-plus-output totals. Primary efficiency uses complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment.
metrics.elapsed: Monotonic wall time for the whole fresh session, including parent-owned public builds and repairs but excluding dependency installation.
metrics.maintainability: Changed editable files, rough token edit size, and whether maintenance patches touch exactly the predeclared defect-root file set.
metrics.source: Final and seed UTF-8 bytes, physical lines, rough tokens, o200k_base tokens, and per-file SHA-256, reported descriptively rather than substituted for session tokens.
metrics.cross_target: HTTP/browser equality for the shared scalar contract plus explicit successful Chromium execution in public and hidden judgments.

primary_gate.execution_integrity: All 96 cells must finish exactly once with unique thread IDs, exactly one journal start/finish, intact repository/toolchain/checker/read-only/FIFO state including post-build hashes, compliant commands, required public HTTP/browser execution, no runner error, and no selective rerun or exclusion.
primary_gate.correctness: Parley must pass 100% of hidden cases and its assignment success rate must be no lower than every baseline overall, within each agent configuration, and within implementation and maintenance tasks.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley's first-public-check assignment success rate must be no lower than the highest baseline rate overall and within each task kind.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley's median complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley's median elapsed seconds per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.maintainability: Every hidden-correct Parley maintenance assignment must change exactly its predeclared root file set, and its exact-root rate must be no lower than every baseline.
primary_gate.verdict: All six conditions must hold for strict unseen full-stack agent parity/efficiency. Report every condition independently even when the overall gate fails.

secondary_analysis: Report full distributions, paired task/configuration/replicate cells, and per-task outcomes; do not replace the primary result with successful, repair-free, or model-selected subsets.
Report implementation and maintenance separately, including root-file quality, public/hidden HTTP-browser execution, and disagreement classes.
Report both model configurations separately before any pooled interpretation.
Report public-attempt counts and public case executions so a build-only or browser-skipped check cannot be mistaken for semantic feedback.
Report post-build protected/read-only hash checks by language and build phase; do not collapse them into only the final workspace flag.
Compare studies 036 and 037 only as motivation and mechanism history. Do not combine their task results, tokens, or timing with 038.
Classify failures after preserving the frozen outcome; classification cannot change a verdict.
interpretation_boundary: The study covers four small synthetic server-plus-browser contracts, two model IDs, one reasoning setting, and one frozen toolchain environment.
Stack scaffolds test application work, not greenfield framework discovery, dependency selection, deployment, sustained load, authentication, databases, accessibility, or production operations.
Framework source and compiler implementations are infrastructure. Their application-facing context is preserved, while complete session tokens remain the primary cost.
A deterministic scalar ES-module export exercised in real Chromium is a cross-target behavior check, not a general user-interface evaluation.
Synthetic maintenance defects measure the declared boundary behaviors and do not estimate the distribution of production defects.
Even a fully passing gate cannot prove universal language superiority; it supports only the frozen comparative claim.
A failed strict gate remains useful evidence and cannot be repaired by same-corpus language, skill, prompt, task, runner, threshold, or metric tuning.
protocol.implementation_rule: Scaffolds, reference applications, dependency preparation, and the runner are implemented only after this protocol commit. Their exact hashes and clean-room reference evidence must be committed in a final pre-measurement execution freeze. No measured session may start before that checkpoint.
protocol.change_rule: From corpus commit b08401e6972822ed211cf33e089b9a59602ea23d onward, no task, case, expected value, language semantics, compiler, skill, web reference, metric, threshold, model, reasoning setting, replicate count, or primary gate may change based on scaffolds, reference code, validation, smoke checks, or measured output. An objective harness defect may be corrected only before measured execution in a documented zero-session amendment preserving old commits and semantic hashes.
protocol.stop_rule: Run every frozen cell once, preserve and publish the complete result whether positive, mixed, negative, or invalid, and make no same-corpus optimization or rerun. Any later language or product change requires an independently frozen corpus outside iteration 038.

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    adult_count: int = Field(ge=0); youth_count: int = Field(ge=0); vehicle_count: int = Field(ge=0); peak_departure: bool
def traveller_total(adults: int, youths: int) -> int: return 0
def passenger_charge(adults: int, youths: int) -> int: return 0
def vehicle_charge(vehicles: int) -> int: return 0
def peak_charge(adults: int, youths: int, vehicles: int, peak: bool) -> int: return 0
def manifest_charge(adults: int, youths: int, vehicles: int, peak: bool) -> int: return 0
def handle(value: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    travellers = traveller_total(value.adult_count, value.youth_count); vehicle = vehicle_charge(value.vehicle_count)
    mode = "mixed" if value.vehicle_count > 0 and travellers > 0 else "vehicle" if value.vehicle_count > 0 else "foot"
    return {"traveller_total": travellers, "passenger_charge_cents": passenger_charge(value.adult_count, value.youth_count), "vehicle_charge_cents": vehicle, "peak_charge_cents": peak_charge(value.adult_count, value.youth_count, value.vehicle_count, value.peak_departure), "manifest_charge_cents": manifest_charge(value.adult_count, value.youth_count, value.vehicle_count, value.peak_departure), "boarding_load": travellers + value.vehicle_count * 3, "travel_mode": mode}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a ferry manifest charge service across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Ferry Manifest contract in the supplied stack. traveller_total is adult_count + youth_count. passenger_charge_cents is adult_count * 1100 + youth_count * 650. vehicle_charge_cents is vehicle_count * 2400. peak_charge_cents is traveller_total * 125 + vehicle_count * 350 during a peak_departure and zero otherwise. manifest_charge_cents is the sum of passenger, vehicle, and peak charges. boarding_load is traveller_total + vehicle_count * 3. travel_mode is mixed when both travellers and vehicles are present, vehicle when only vehicles are present, and foot otherwise. The browser export returns manifest_charge_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Ferry Manifest","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/ferry-manifest` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `adult_count`: number
- `youth_count`: number
- `vehicle_count`: number
- `peak_departure`: yesno

Response fields:

- `traveller_total`: number
- `passenger_charge_cents`: number
- `vehicle_charge_cents`: number
- `peak_charge_cents`: number
- `manifest_charge_cents`: number
- `boarding_load`: number
- `travel_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `manifest_charge` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`manifest_charge_cents` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/live")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Ferry Manifest", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v2/ferry-manifest")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a ferry manifest charge service across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Ferry Manifest contract in the supplied stack. traveller_total is adult_count + youth_count. passenger_charge_cents is adult_count * 1100 + youth_count * 650. vehicle_charge_cents is vehicle_count * 2400. peak_charge_cents is traveller_total * 125 + vehicle_count * 350 during a peak_departure and zero otherwise. manifest_charge_cents is the sum of passenger, vehicle, and peak charges. boarding_load is traveller_total + vehicle_count * 3. travel_mode is mixed when both travellers and vehicles are present, vehicle when only vehicles are present, and foot otherwise. The browser export returns manifest_charge_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Ferry Manifest","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/ferry-manifest` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `adult_count`: number
- `youth_count`: number
- `vehicle_count`: number
- `peak_departure`: yesno

Response fields:

- `traveller_total`: number
- `passenger_charge_cents`: number
- `vehicle_charge_cents`: number
- `peak_charge_cents`: number
- `manifest_charge_cents`: number
- `boarding_load`: number
- `travel_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `manifest_charge` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`manifest_charge_cents` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub adult_count:i64,pub youth_count:i64,pub vehicle_count:i64,pub peak_departure:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.adult_count>=0&&self.youth_count>=0&&self.vehicle_count>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub traveller_total:i64,pub passenger_charge_cents:i64,pub vehicle_charge_cents:i64,pub peak_charge_cents:i64,pub manifest_charge_cents:i64,pub boarding_load:i64,pub travel_mode:String}
pub fn manifest_charge(a:i64,y:i64,v:i64,p:bool)->i64{0}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let travellers=x.adult_count+x.youth_count;let passenger=x.adult_count*1100+x.youth_count*650;let vehicle=x.vehicle_count*2400;let peak=if x.peak_departure{travellers*125+x.vehicle_count*350}else{0};let mode=if x.vehicle_count>0{if travellers>0{"mixed"}else{"vehicle"}}else{"foot"};ResponseOutput{traveller_total:travellers,passenger_charge_cents:passenger,vehicle_charge_cents:vehicle,peak_charge_cents:peak,manifest_charge_cents:manifest_charge(x.adult_count,x.youth_count,x.vehicle_count,x.peak_departure),boarding_load:travellers+x.vehicle_count*3,travel_mode:mode.into()}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_manifest_charge(a:i64,y:i64,v:i64,p:i32)->i64{manifest_charge(a,y,v,p!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_038::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { manifest_charge: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_manifest_charge(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Ferry Manifest", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_038_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/live", get(status)).route("/api/v2/ferry-manifest", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Build a ferry manifest charge service across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Ferry Manifest contract in the supplied stack. traveller_total is adult_count + youth_count. passenger_charge_cents is adult_count * 1100 + youth_count * 650. vehicle_charge_cents is vehicle_count * 2400. peak_charge_cents is traveller_total * 125 + vehicle_count * 350 during a peak_departure and zero otherwise. manifest_charge_cents is the sum of passenger, vehicle, and peak charges. boarding_load is traveller_total + vehicle_count * 3. travel_mode is mixed when both travellers and vehicles are present, vehicle when only vehicles are present, and foot otherwise. The browser export returns manifest_charge_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Ferry Manifest","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/ferry-manifest` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `adult_count`: number
- `youth_count`: number
- `vehicle_count`: number
- `peak_departure`: yesno

Response fields:

- `traveller_total`: number
- `passenger_charge_cents`: number
- `vehicle_charge_cents`: number
- `peak_charge_cents`: number
- `manifest_charge_cents`: number
- `boarding_load`: number
- `travel_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `manifest_charge` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`manifest_charge_cents` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub adult_count:i64,pub youth_count:i64,pub vehicle_count:i64,pub peak_departure:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.adult_count>=0&&self.youth_count>=0&&self.vehicle_count>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub traveller_total:i64,pub passenger_charge_cents:i64,pub vehicle_charge_cents:i64,pub peak_charge_cents:i64,pub manifest_charge_cents:i64,pub boarding_load:i64,pub travel_mode:String}
pub fn manifest_charge(a:i64,y:i64,v:i64,p:bool)->i64{0}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let travellers=x.adult_count+x.youth_count;let passenger=x.adult_count*1100+x.youth_count*650;let vehicle=x.vehicle_count*2400;let peak=if x.peak_departure{travellers*125+x.vehicle_count*350}else{0};let mode=if x.vehicle_count>0{if travellers>0{"mixed"}else{"vehicle"}}else{"foot"};ResponseOutput{traveller_total:travellers,passenger_charge_cents:passenger,vehicle_charge_cents:vehicle,peak_charge_cents:peak,manifest_charge_cents:manifest_charge(x.adult_count,x.youth_count,x.vehicle_count,x.peak_departure),boarding_load:travellers+x.vehicle_count*3,travel_mode:mode.into()}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_manifest_charge(a:i64,y:i64,v:i64,p:i32)->i64{manifest_charge(a,y,v,p!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_038::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { manifest_charge: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_manifest_charge(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Ferry Manifest", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_038_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/live", get(status)).route("/api/v2/ferry-manifest", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

logic.par.text:
to corrected_degrees with measured_degrees as number, door_open as yesno giving number:
    if door_open:
        give back measured_degrees plus 2
    give back measured_degrees
to required_cooling with measured_degrees as number, target_degrees as number, allowed_drift as number, door_open as yesno giving number:
    let excess be (corrected_degrees with measured_degrees, door_open) minus target_degrees minus allowed_drift
    if excess is less than 0:
        set excess to 0
    give back number from ((excess plus 2) divided by 3)

main.par.text:
include "logic.par"
a cold_request has measured_degrees as number, target_degrees as number, allowed_drift as number, door_open as yesno
a cold_response has corrected_degrees as number, temperature_gap as number, excess_heat as number, cooling_steps as number, safe_flag as yesno, storage_condition as text
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Cold Storage", ready yes
to handle_request with request as cold_request giving cold_response:
    let corrected be (corrected_degrees with request's measured_degrees, request's door_open)
    let gap be corrected minus request's target_degrees
    if gap is less than 0:
        set gap to 0 minus gap
    let excess be corrected minus request's target_degrees minus request's allowed_drift
    if excess is less than 0:
        set excess to 0
    let steps be (required_cooling with request's measured_degrees, request's target_degrees, request's allowed_drift, request's door_open)
    let safe be no
    let condition be "warming"
    if gap is less than request's allowed_drift plus 1:
        set safe to yes
        set condition to "stable"
    otherwise:
        if corrected is more than request's target_degrees:
            set condition to "cooling"
    give back a cold_response with corrected_degrees corrected, temperature_gap gap, excess_heat excess, cooling_steps steps, safe_flag safe, storage_condition condition

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair door-open correction in a cold-storage evaluator

Repair the supplied Cold Storage application. corrected_degrees is measured_degrees + 2 when door_open is true and measured_degrees otherwise. temperature_gap is the absolute difference between corrected_degrees and target_degrees. excess_heat is max(corrected_degrees - target_degrees - allowed_drift, 0). cooling_steps divides excess_heat into three-degree steps using ceiling division, with zero excess heat producing zero steps. safe_flag is true when temperature_gap is at most allowed_drift. storage_condition is stable when safe_flag is true, cooling when corrected_degrees is above target_degrees, and warming otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns cooling_steps.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Cold Storage","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/cold-storage` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `measured_degrees`: number
- `target_degrees`: number
- `allowed_drift`: number
- `door_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `corrected_degrees`: number
- `temperature_gap`: number
- `excess_heat`: number
- `cooling_steps`: number
- `safe_flag`: yesno
- `storage_condition`: text

## Browser

Export `required_cooling` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`cooling_steps` for equivalent inputs.

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair reward derivation after claimed loyalty stamps

Repair the supplied Loyalty Stamps application. base_stamps is purchase_count * stamps_each. bonus_stamps is purchase_count during a double_day and zero otherwise. spendable_stamps is max(base_stamps + bonus_stamps - claimed_stamps, 0). reward_count is spendable_stamps divided by 10 using floor division. leftover_stamps is spendable_stamps modulo 10. reward_stage is ready when reward_count is positive and collecting otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns reward_count.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Loyalty Stamps","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/loyalty-stamps` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `purchase_count`: number
- `stamps_each`: number
- `claimed_stamps`: number
- `double_day`: yesno

Response fields:

- `base_stamps`: number
- `bonus_stamps`: number
- `spendable_stamps`: number
- `reward_count`: number
- `leftover_stamps`: number
- `reward_stage`: text

## Browser

Export `claimable_rewards` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`reward_count` for equivalent inputs.

===== logic.par [editable] =====
to base_stamps with purchase_count as number, stamps_each as number giving number:
    give back purchase_count times stamps_each
to bonus_stamps with purchase_count as number, double_day as yesno giving number:
    if double_day:
        give back purchase_count
    give back 0
to spendable_stamps with purchase_count as number, stamps_each as number, claimed_stamps as number, double_day as yesno giving number:
    let spendable be (base_stamps with purchase_count, stamps_each) plus (bonus_stamps with purchase_count, double_day) minus claimed_stamps
    if spendable is less than 0:
        give back 0
    give back spendable
to claimable_rewards with purchase_count as number, stamps_each as number, claimed_stamps as number, double_day as yesno giving number:
    let earned be (base_stamps with purchase_count, stamps_each) plus (bonus_stamps with purchase_count, double_day)
    give back number from (earned divided by 10)
===== main.par [editable] =====
include "logic.par"
a loyalty_request has purchase_count as number, stamps_each as number, claimed_stamps as number, double_day as yesno
a loyalty_response has base_stamps as number, bonus_stamps as number, spendable_stamps as number, reward_count as number, leftover_stamps as number, reward_stage as text
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Loyalty Stamps", ready yes
to handle_request with request as loyalty_request giving loyalty_response:
    let base be (base_stamps with request's purchase_count, request's stamps_each)
    let bonus be (bonus_stamps with request's purchase_count, request's double_day)
    let spendable be (spendable_stamps with request's purchase_count, request's stamps_each, request's claimed_stamps, request's double_day)
    let rewards be (claimable_rewards with request's purchase_count, request's stamps_each, request's claimed_stamps, request's double_day)
    let stage be "collecting"
    if rewards is more than 0:
        set stage to "ready"
    give back a loyalty_response with base_stamps base, bonus_stamps bonus, spendable_stamps spendable, reward_count rewards, leftover_stamps spendable minus rewards times 10, reward_stage stage

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build an archive retention index across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Archive Retention contract in the supplied stack. page_total is document_count * pages_each. base_months is requested_years * 12. retained_months is max(base_months, 84) during a legal_hold and base_months otherwise. review_batches divides page_total into 200-page batches using ceiling division, with zero pages producing zero batches. retention_score is retained_months + review_batches * 3. retention_class is held during a legal_hold and standard otherwise. The browser export returns retention_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Archive Retention","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/archive-retention` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `document_count`: number
- `pages_each`: number
- `requested_years`: number
- `legal_hold`: yesno

Response fields:

- `page_total`: number
- `base_months`: number
- `retained_months`: number
- `review_batches`: number
- `retention_score`: number
- `retention_class`: text

## Browser

Export `retention_index` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`retention_score` for equivalent inputs.

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair door-open correction in a cold-storage evaluator

Repair the supplied Cold Storage application. corrected_degrees is measured_degrees + 2 when door_open is true and measured_degrees otherwise. temperature_gap is the absolute difference between corrected_degrees and target_degrees. excess_heat is max(corrected_degrees - target_degrees - allowed_drift, 0). cooling_steps divides excess_heat into three-degree steps using ceiling division, with zero excess heat producing zero steps. safe_flag is true when temperature_gap is at most allowed_drift. storage_condition is stable when safe_flag is true, cooling when corrected_degrees is above target_degrees, and warming otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns cooling_steps.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Cold Storage","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/cold-storage` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `measured_degrees`: number
- `target_degrees`: number
- `allowed_drift`: number
- `door_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `corrected_degrees`: number
- `temperature_gap`: number
- `excess_heat`: number
- `cooling_steps`: number
- `safe_flag`: yesno
- `storage_condition`: text

## Browser

Export `required_cooling` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`cooling_steps` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub measured_degrees:i64,pub target_degrees:i64,pub allowed_drift:i64,pub door_open:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.measured_degrees>=0&&self.target_degrees>=0&&self.allowed_drift>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub corrected_degrees:i64,pub temperature_gap:i64,pub excess_heat:i64,pub cooling_steps:i64,pub safe_flag:bool,pub storage_condition:String}
pub fn corrected_degrees(m:i64,d:bool)->i64{m}
pub fn required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:bool)->i64{((corrected_degrees(m,d)-t-a).max(0)+2)/3}

# Repair door-open correction in a cold-storage evaluator

Repair the supplied Cold Storage application. corrected_degrees is measured_degrees + 2 when door_open is true and measured_degrees otherwise. temperature_gap is the absolute difference between corrected_degrees and target_degrees. excess_heat is max(corrected_degrees - target_degrees - allowed_drift, 0). cooling_steps divides excess_heat into three-degree steps using ceiling division, with zero excess heat producing zero steps. safe_flag is true when temperature_gap is at most allowed_drift. storage_condition is stable when safe_flag is true, cooling when corrected_degrees is above target_degrees, and warming otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns cooling_steps.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Cold Storage","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/cold-storage` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `measured_degrees`: number
- `target_degrees`: number
- `allowed_drift`: number
- `door_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `corrected_degrees`: number
- `temperature_gap`: number
- `excess_heat`: number
- `cooling_steps`: number
- `safe_flag`: yesno
- `storage_condition`: text

## Browser

Export `required_cooling` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`cooling_steps` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub measured_degrees:i64,pub target_degrees:i64,pub allowed_drift:i64,pub door_open:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.measured_degrees>=0&&self.target_degrees>=0&&self.allowed_drift>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub corrected_degrees:i64,pub temperature_gap:i64,pub excess_heat:i64,pub cooling_steps:i64,pub safe_flag:bool,pub storage_condition:String}
pub fn corrected_degrees(m:i64,d:bool)->i64{m}
pub fn required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:bool)->i64{((corrected_degrees(m,d)-t-a).max(0)+2)/3}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let corrected=corrected_degrees(x.measured_degrees,x.door_open);let gap=(corrected-x.target_degrees).abs();let excess=(corrected-x.target_degrees-x.allowed_drift).max(0);let safe=gap<=x.allowed_drift;ResponseOutput{corrected_degrees:corrected,temperature_gap:gap,excess_heat:excess,cooling_steps:required_cooling(x.measured_degrees,x.target_degrees,x.allowed_drift,x.door_open),safe_flag:safe,storage_condition:if safe{"stable".into()}else if corrected>x.target_degrees{"cooling".into()}else{"warming".into()}}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:i32)->i64{required_cooling(m,t,a,d!=0)}

use fullstack_agent_038::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { required_cooling: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_required_cooling(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Cold Storage", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_038_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/live", get(status)).route("/api/v2/cold-storage", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a ferry manifest charge service across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Ferry Manifest contract in the supplied stack. traveller_total is adult_count + youth_count. passenger_charge_cents is adult_count * 1100 + youth_count * 650. vehicle_charge_cents is vehicle_count * 2400. peak_charge_cents is traveller_total * 125 + vehicle_count * 350 during a peak_departure and zero otherwise. manifest_charge_cents is the sum of passenger, vehicle, and peak charges. boarding_load is traveller_total + vehicle_count * 3. travel_mode is mixed when both travellers and vehicles are present, vehicle when only vehicles are present, and foot otherwise. The browser export returns manifest_charge_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Ferry Manifest","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/ferry-manifest` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `adult_count`: number
- `youth_count`: number

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub purchase_count:i64,pub stamps_each:i64,pub claimed_stamps:i64,pub double_day:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.purchase_count>=0&&self.stamps_each>=0&&self.claimed_stamps>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub base_stamps:i64,pub bonus_stamps:i64,pub spendable_stamps:i64,pub reward_count:i64,pub leftover_stamps:i64,pub reward_stage:String}
pub fn claimable_rewards(p:i64,e:i64,c:i64,d:bool)->i64{(p*e+if d{p}else{0})/10}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let base=x.purchase_count*x.stamps_each;let bonus=if x.double_day{x.purchase_count}else{0};let spendable=(base+bonus-x.claimed_stamps).max(0);let rewards=claimable_rewards(x.purchase_count,x.stamps_each,x.claimed_stamps,x.double_day);ResponseOutput{base_stamps:base,bonus_stamps:bonus,spendable_stamps:spendable,reward_count:rewards,leftover_stamps:spendable-rewards*10,reward_stage:if rewards>0{"ready".into()}else{"collecting".into()}}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_claimable_rewards(p:i64,e:i64,c:i64,d:i32)->i64{claimable_rewards(p,e,c,d!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_038::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { claimable_rewards: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_claimable_rewards(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Loyalty Stamps", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_038_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/live", get(status)).route("/api/v2/loyalty-stamps", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Repair reward derivation after claimed loyalty stamps

Repair the supplied Loyalty Stamps application. base_stamps is purchase_count * stamps_each. bonus_stamps is purchase_count during a double_day and zero otherwise. spendable_stamps is max(base_stamps + bonus_stamps - claimed_stamps, 0). reward_count is spendable_stamps divided by 10 using floor division. leftover_stamps is spendable_stamps modulo 10. reward_stage is ready when reward_count is positive and collecting otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns reward_count.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Loyalty Stamps","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/loyalty-stamps` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `purchase_count`: number
- `stamps_each`: number
- `claimed_stamps`: number
- `double_day`: yesno

Response fields:

- `base_stamps`: number
- `bonus_stamps`: number
- `spendable_stamps`: number
- `reward_count`: number
- `leftover_stamps`: number
- `reward_stage`: text

## Browser

Export `claimable_rewards` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`reward_count` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub purchase_count:i64,pub stamps_each:i64,pub claimed_stamps:i64,pub double_day:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.purchase_count>=0&&self.stamps_each>=0&&self.claimed_stamps>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub base_stamps:i64,pub bonus_stamps:i64,pub spendable_stamps:i64,pub reward_count:i64,pub leftover_stamps:i64,pub reward_stage:String}
pub fn claimable_rewards(p:i64,e:i64,c:i64,d:bool)->i64{(p*e+if d{p}else{0})/10}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let base=x.purchase_count*x.stamps_each;let bonus=if x.double_day{x.purchase_count}else{0};let spendable=(base+bonus-x.claimed_stamps).max(0);let rewards=claimable_rewards(x.purchase_count,x.stamps_each,x.claimed_stamps,x.double_day);ResponseOutput{base_stamps:base,bonus_stamps:bonus,spendable_stamps:spendable,reward_count:rewards,leftover_stamps:spendable-rewards*10,reward_stage:if rewards>0{"ready".into()}else{"collecting".into()}}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_claimable_rewards(p:i64,e:i64,c:i64,d:i32)->i64{claimable_rewards(p,e,c,d!=0)}

# Repair door-open correction in a cold-storage evaluator

Repair the supplied Cold Storage application. corrected_degrees is measured_degrees + 2 when door_open is true and measured_degrees otherwise. temperature_gap is the absolute difference between corrected_degrees and target_degrees. excess_heat is max(corrected_degrees - target_degrees - allowed_drift, 0). cooling_steps divides excess_heat into three-degree steps using ceiling division, with zero excess heat producing zero steps. safe_flag is true when temperature_gap is at most allowed_drift. storage_condition is stable when safe_flag is true, cooling when corrected_degrees is above target_degrees, and warming otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns cooling_steps.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Cold Storage","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/cold-storage` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `measured_degrees`: number
- `target_degrees`: number
- `allowed_drift`: number
- `door_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `corrected_degrees`: number
- `temperature_gap`: number
- `excess_heat`: number
- `cooling_steps`: number
- `safe_flag`: yesno
- `storage_condition`: text

## Browser

Export `required_cooling` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`cooling_steps` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub measured_degrees:i64,pub target_degrees:i64,pub allowed_drift:i64,pub door_open:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.measured_degrees>=0&&self.target_degrees>=0&&self.allowed_drift>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub corrected_degrees:i64,pub temperature_gap:i64,pub excess_heat:i64,pub cooling_steps:i64,pub safe_flag:bool,pub storage_condition:String}
pub fn corrected_degrees(m:i64,d:bool)->i64{m}
pub fn required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:bool)->i64{((corrected_degrees(m,d)-t-a).max(0)+2)/3}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let corrected=corrected_degrees(x.measured_degrees,x.door_open);let gap=(corrected-x.target_degrees).abs();let excess=(corrected-x.target_degrees-x.allowed_drift).max(0);let safe=gap<=x.allowed_drift;ResponseOutput{corrected_degrees:corrected,temperature_gap:gap,excess_heat:excess,cooling_steps:required_cooling(x.measured_degrees,x.target_degrees,x.allowed_drift,x.door_open),safe_flag:safe,storage_condition:if safe{"stable".into()}else if corrected>x.target_degrees{"cooling".into()}else{"warming".into()}}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:i32)->i64{required_cooling(m,t,a,d!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_038::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { required_cooling: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_required_cooling(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Cold Storage", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_038_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/live", get(status)).route("/api/v2/cold-storage", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Repair door-open correction in a cold-storage evaluator

Repair the supplied Cold Storage application. corrected_degrees is measured_degrees + 2 when door_open is true and measured_degrees otherwise. temperature_gap is the absolute difference between corrected_degrees and target_degrees. excess_heat is max(corrected_degrees - target_degrees - allowed_drift, 0). cooling_steps divides excess_heat into three-degree steps using ceiling division, with zero excess heat producing zero steps. safe_flag is true when temperature_gap is at most allowed_drift. storage_condition is stable when safe_flag is true, cooling when corrected_degrees is above target_degrees, and warming otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns cooling_steps.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Cold Storage","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/cold-storage` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `measured_degrees`: number
- `target_degrees`: number
- `allowed_drift`: number
- `door_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `corrected_degrees`: number
- `temperature_gap`: number
- `excess_heat`: number
- `cooling_steps`: number
- `safe_flag`: yesno
- `storage_condition`: text

## Browser

Export `required_cooling` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`cooling_steps` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub measured_degrees:i64,pub target_degrees:i64,pub allowed_drift:i64,pub door_open:bool}
impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.measured_degrees>=0&&self.target_degrees>=0&&self.allowed_drift>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub corrected_degrees:i64,pub temperature_gap:i64,pub excess_heat:i64,pub cooling_steps:i64,pub safe_flag:bool,pub storage_condition:String}
pub fn corrected_degrees(m:i64,d:bool)->i64{m}
pub fn required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:bool)->i64{((corrected_degrees(m,d)-t-a).max(0)+2)/3}
pub fn handle(x:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let corrected=corrected_degrees(x.measured_degrees,x.door_open);let gap=(corrected-x.target_degrees).abs();let excess=(corrected-x.target_degrees-x.allowed_drift).max(0);let safe=gap<=x.allowed_drift;ResponseOutput{corrected_degrees:corrected,temperature_gap:gap,excess_heat:excess,cooling_steps:required_cooling(x.measured_degrees,x.target_degrees,x.allowed_drift,x.door_open),safe_flag:safe,storage_condition:if safe{"stable".into()}else if corrected>x.target_degrees{"cooling".into()}else{"warming".into()}}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_required_cooling(m:i64,t:i64,a:i64,d:i32)->i64{required_cooling(m,t,a,d!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_038::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { required_cooling: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_required_cooling(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Cold Storage", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_038_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/live", get(status)).route("/api/v2/cold-storage", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_038.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

to corrected_degrees with measured_degrees as number, door_open as yesno giving number:
    if door_open:
        give back measured_degrees plus 2
    give back measured_degrees
to required_cooling with measured_degrees as number, target_degrees as number, allowed_drift as number, door_open as yesno giving number:

        set excess to 0
    give back number from ((excess plus 2) divided by 3)

main.par.text:
include "logic.par"
a cold_request has measured_degrees as number, target_degrees as number, allowed_drift as number, door_open as yesno
a cold_response has corrected_degrees as number, temperature_gap as number, excess_heat as number, cooling_steps as number, safe_flag as yesno, storage_condition as text
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Cold Storage", ready yes
to handle_request with request as cold_request giving cold_response:
    let corrected be (corrected_degrees with request's measured_degrees, request's door_open)
    let gap be corrected minus request's target_degrees
    if gap is less than 0:
        set gap to 0 minus gap
    let excess be corrected minus request's target_degrees minus request's allowed_drift
    if excess is less than 0:
        set excess to 0
    let steps be (required_cooling with request's measured_degrees, request's target_degrees, request's allowed_drift, request's door_open)
    let safe be no
    let condition be "warming"
    if gap is less than request's allowed_drift plus 1:
        set safe to yes
        set condition to "stable"
    otherwise:
        if corrected is more than request's target_degrees:
            set condition to "cooling"
    give back a cold_response with corrected_degrees corrected, temperature_gap gap, excess_heat excess, cooling_steps steps, safe_flag safe, storage_condition condition

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair door-open correction in a cold-storage evaluator

Repair the supplied Cold Storage application. corrected_degrees is measured_degrees + 2 when door_open is true and measured_degrees otherwise. temperature_gap is the absolute difference between corrected_degrees and target_degrees. excess_heat is max(corrected_degrees - target_degrees - allowed_drift, 0). cooling_steps divides excess_heat into three-degree steps using ceiling division, with zero excess heat producing zero steps. safe_flag is true when temperature_gap is at most allowed_drift. storage_condition is stable when safe_flag is true, cooling when corrected_degrees is above target_degrees, and warming otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns cooling_steps.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/live` returns `{"service":"Cold Storage","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v2/cold-storage` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `measured_degrees`: number
- `target_degrees`: number
- `allowed_drift`: number
- `door_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `corrected_degrees`: number
- `temperature_gap`: number
- `excess_heat`: number
- `cooling_steps`: number
- `safe_flag`: yesno
- `storage_condition`: text

## Browser

Export `required_cooling` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`cooling_steps` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/live")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Cold Storage", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v2/cold-storage")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    measured_degrees: int = Field(ge=0); target_degrees: int = Field(ge=0); allowed_drift: int = Field(ge=0); door_open: bool
def corrected_degrees(measured: int, door: bool) -> int: return measured
def handle(value: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    corrected = corrected_degrees(value.measured_degrees, value.door_open); gap = abs(corrected - value.target_degrees); excess = max(corrected - value.target_degrees - value.allowed_drift, 0); steps = (excess + 2) // 3; safe = gap <= value.allowed_drift
    return {"corrected_degrees": corrected, "temperature_gap": gap, "excess_heat": excess, "cooling_steps": steps, "safe_flag": safe, "storage_condition": "stable" if safe else "cooling" if corrected > value.target_degrees else "warming"}
